The Lives of the Queens of England is a multi-volumed work attributed to Agnes Strickland, though it was mostly researched and written by her sister Elisabeth. These volumes give biographies of the queens of England from the Norman Conquest in 1066.

Conjunto de cuentos cortos y leyendas nativas al área del río Paraná (Sur de Brasil, Norte de Argentina), con toques descriptivos de la vida indígena y las pasiones humanas. (Introducción por Mario Pineda. Revisado por vviera y mpinedag)

The story, set in the 17th Century during the reign of Louis XIII in France, concerns the progress of an impoverished nobleman as he ventures forth into a series of dangerous adventures which culminate in the restoration of his true noble social position. In today's parlance the story might be described as an action romance.
Charles Moray is jilted on the eve of his wedding. He then leaves the country for a few years.

A relatively short, autobiographical account of the life of Calvin Coolidge, 30th president of the United States of America. The contents span from Coolidge's childhood to the conclusion of his second term as president.
Science fiction is a genre encompassing imaginative works that take place in this world or that of the author’s creation where anything is possible. The only rules are those set forth by the author.

The Story of Gisli the Outlaw is a translation of the medieval Icelandic Gísla saga súrssonar, the tale of a family feud and of Gísli's attempts to evade his enemies as an outlaw. (Summary by Alison Sawers)

A 1903 reprint of a volume published in 1856, edited by Lyman Draper. Contents recorded include: three memoirs of early 19th century Wisconsin, a description of pioneer life, articles about the Black Hawk War, an account of the immigration of the Stockbridge Indians from New York, a portrait of early Mineral Point and nearby Richland County, and a few other shorter articles.

Jessie Pope published these poems during the early months of the First World War. They were very popular at the time and the author received many letters of support and gratitude including some from men serving at the Front.

Freeman Wills Crofts was part of the golden age of detective fiction, along with the likes of Agatha Christie and Raymond Chandler. His most famous creation, Inspector Joseph French of Scotland Yard, appeared in more than 30 novels between 1924 and 1957.

Die Pickwickier (The Posthumous Papers of the Pickwick Club)** von Charles Dickens (1836–37) ist der erste Roman des Autors und ein humorvolles, episodisches Werk, das gesellschaftliche Satire mit skurrilen Charakteren verbindet. Die Geschichte folgt **Samuel Pickwick**, dem gutmütigen Gründer des Pickwick Clubs, und seinen drei exzentrischen Freunden – **Tracy Tupman**, **Augustus Snodgrass** und **Nathaniel Winkle*

This is the 41st Coffee Break Collection, in which Librivox readers select and read stories or poems, fiction or non-fiction pieces of fifteen minutes' duration or less, suitable for short commutes and coffee breaks. The subject for this collection is "WITCHCRAFT", including spells, rituals, persecution of witches, druids, etc.

This work is a collection of tales told by Elders in a Blackfoot lodge centered around the tribe. In addition to the traditional stories and adventures there are stories about the cultural practices that reflect their societal values and historical experiences.

A play written late in Pinero's career that shows he still knew how to reach his audience. A wounded WW1 veteran discovers that love truly conquers all in the Enchanted Cottage.

The Wisconsin Historical Society was founded in 1846, even before Wisconsin achieved U.S. statehood. The Secretary, Lyman Draper, began in the early 1850s to solicit articles from around the state containing early impressions and descriptions of original pioneer settlers.

The English poet John Clare was the son of a farm labourer and was often referred to as "the Northamptonshire Peasant Poet". His work is mostly inspired by the English countryside and the rural way of life.

Jane Ellen Harrison was an English classical scholar whose work had a particular focus on the earliest origins of Greek religion. Her Mythology is a popular rather than an academic book, and its subject is the psychological/cultural history and “purpose” of the chief Olympian gods and certain other mythological creatures, both for the ancient Greeks themselves, and through history to the present day.

Winnebago Stories is a collection of traditional tales from the Winnebago (Ho-Chunk) tribe, offering insight into the rich oral traditions of the Winnebago people. The book also delves into the creation myths, Heroic tales, clan organization and significance of various Winnebago clans, as well as customs related to birth, death, marriage, and naming ceremonies. (Summary by Kirk)
